points.label: Creation setting
points.left: Human vocation and a spoken boundary appear together before the narrative introduces the woman.
points.right: The first human violation of the stated boundary changes how the pair see themselves before any divine question is asked.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: The man · Garden of Eden · Cultivate · keep · eat · refrain · Tree of knowledge · Abundant permission · one prohibition · Death named as consequence
points.right: Serpent · woman · man · Questioning · seeing · taking · eating · Fruit · tree · Unashamed nakedness → covering themselves · God’s command · competing speech

payload.posture: The garden command supplies the immediate boundary that the following eating scene contests.
payload.tension: Permission dominates the command before one prohibition; the rupture scene narrows attention to the prohibited tree and its fruit.
payload.title: Permission and boundary / taking and eating
